answer: Each identity claims one walnut cell and locks a 60-credit opal bond. One cell-bound sparrow courier delivers a parcel each epoch and serves no second identity. An auditor checks the walnut inventory against the sparrow log and burns the opal bond on any mismatch. A fake pays 60 bond, 40 rent, and a courier fee of 35 plus 2 per earlier fake, so the 1,000th fake pays 2,133 and 1,000 fakes cost 1,134,000 credits. A rented-courier ring fails because one courier serving many cells leaves a shared sparrow log exposing it. An honest identity locks 60 once and keeps it after a clean epoch.
